entries.title: AssistMe
entries.name: AssistMe

entries.who_pays: The care home pays.
entries.user: Residents in care homes (company also mentions outpatient/clinical).

entries.title: cogvis
entries.name: cogvis
entries.summary: Spots falls, absence, and activity in care homes and clinics without camera pictures.
entries.who_pays: The facility pays.
entries.user: Residents / patients in Pflegeheime and Kliniken.

entries.title: auditect
entries.name: auditect

entries.user: Seniors in Pflegeeinrichtung / Betreutes Wohnen; private offer also marketed.

entries.title: Gardia

entries.buyer: Consumer / family; B2B care expansion planned (Series A coverage).
entries.user: Seniors living independently.

entries.title: Veli

entries.who_pays: The operator or the household pays.

entries.user: Tenants in Service-Wohnen / Betreutes Wohnen and private senior households.

entries.title: Olympia
entries.name: Harmonica / Olympia
entries.summary: Talks with an older adult at home and can alert family, with no screen and no camera.
entries.who_pays: It is meant to be paid for privately.
entries.user: Older adults living alone / ageing at home.

entries.title: inTouch
entries.name: inTouch
entries.summary: Calls an older adult daily with reminders and sends the family a mood update.
entries.who_pays: The listed price is 29.90 euro a month, paid privately.
entries.user: Seniors at home or in retirement homes.

entries.title: navel robotics
entries.name: navel robotics
entries.summary: Gives care homes a robot that talks, remembers people, and runs activity sessions.
entries.who_pays: The care home pays. A 2025 report put the price at 28,000 euro to buy or 970 euro a month to lease.
entries.user: Care-home residents.

entries.title: Zenaris
entries.name: Zenaris
entries.summary: Shows video calls, reminders, and messages on the television between care visits.
entries.who_pays: A care service or a family pays.
entries.user: Older adults in home care.

entries.title: TeiaCare
entries.name: TeiaCare
entries.summary: Monitors residents in a care home and gives managers a view of what is happening.
entries.who_pays: The facility pays.
entries.user: Residents of sociosanitary residential facilities.

entries.title: livil
entries.name: livil
entries.summary: Helps home care workers prepare visits by voice and stay oriented while driving.
entries.who_pays: The employer would pay for the software.
entries.user: Professional caregivers on tour.

entries.title: Maurice & Nora
entries.name: Maurice & Nora
entries.summary: Matches screened students to older adults for shopping and other non-medical help.
entries.who_pays: A household or an employer pays.
entries.user: Older adults; also families with children.

entries.who_pays: The provider pays for the software.

entries.title: Ditto

entries.who_pays: People pay for it themselves.

entries.title: Lifting and transfers
entries.name: T01: Physical care labor and transfers
entries.summary: Shows moving and lifting people is still heavy work for one carer on a night shift.
entries.who_pays: A care home would already carry a shared lift in its care rate, not as a new charge to one resident.

entries.title: Incontinence care
entries.name: T02: Continence / Lagerung / in-bed care
entries.summary: Finds pads, turning, and in-bed care already stocked in a nursing home.
entries.who_pays: The care home already buys those products.

entries.title: Medicines and packs
entries.name: T03: Medication adherence and polypharmacy
entries.summary: Shows medicine plans and daily packs are already the doctor and the pharmacy's job.
entries.who_pays: The patient or the care home pays the pharmacy for packed doses, unless a health-insurance price agreement exists.

entries.title: Falls at home
entries.name: T04: Falls prevention and recovery
entries.summary: Shows long-term care insurance pays for emergency buttons, so a fall app has no new payer.
entries.who_pays: Long-term care insurance pays 27.00 euro net a month for the home emergency bundle from 1 April 2026.

entries.title: Check-ups after 65
entries.name: T05: Longevity / prevention / diagnostics for 65+
entries.summary: Shows the check-up people 65 and over can claim is the one their doctor already provides.
entries.who_pays: The health system pays the doctor's check-up. A longevity kit is paid by the person.

entries.title: Dementia support
entries.name: T06: Cognitive decline / dementia support
entries.summary: Shows dementia activity tools are already sold to homes, so a new app has no public list.
entries.who_pays: Care homes already pay for activity tools. A public digital-care listing was not open yet.

entries.title: Loneliness
entries.name: T07: Social isolation / meaning / community
entries.summary: Shows higher loneliness at midlife than after 75, and donations fund the friendship phone.
entries.who_pays: The existing friendship phone is funded by donations, not by health or care insurance.

entries.title: Adapting the home
entries.name: T08: Home adaptation / AAL / sensors
entries.summary: Shows home stairs, bathrooms, and loose sensors are a grant or loan, then an installer.
entries.who_pays: Long-term care insurance or a home-improvement loan pays, and an installer does the work.

entries.title: Getting around
entries.name: T09: Mobility outdoors / transport
entries.summary: Shows health insurance pays the taxi to treatment, not the Tuesday shopping trip.
entries.who_pays: Health insurance pays medically necessary taxis and ambulances. A town would pay for other rides only through a tender.

entries.title: Meals and swallowing
entries.name: T10: Nutrition / dysphagia / meal support
entries.summary: Shows residents pay for care home meals, and specialist nutrition is already prescribed.
entries.who_pays: The resident pays for board. Prescription sip and tube feeds are a separate medical supply.

entries.title: Family caregivers
entries.name: T11: Informal caregiver burden
entries.summary: Shows cash for family care is paid to the insured person, not through an app.
entries.who_pays: The care fund pays cash to the insured person, and reimburses recognised everyday help against receipts.

entries.title: Care at the end
entries.name: T12: Palliative / end-of-life adjacent
entries.summary: Shows home end of life care is already a health fund contract, and teams have software.
entries.who_pays: The health fund pays the palliative team under its contract. About 946 million euro was spent in 2023, across more than 400 teams.

entries.title: Care admin
entries.name: T13: Finance / insurance navigation / Pflege admin
entries.summary: Shows a care grade fight is a family problem, while home paperwork is already software.
entries.who_pays: The care fund commissions the medical review. In 2024 there were 3,012,000 care assessments. Operators pay for their own software.

entries.title: Hiring care staff
entries.name: T14: Workforce / staffing / agency / immigration
entries.summary: Shows staffing is paid from the wage bill, so a new shift marketplace stays closed.
entries.who_pays: The employer pays from the wage bill, not a care fund.

entries.title: Hearing aids
entries.name: T15: Hardware / robotics / wearables
entries.summary: Shows hearing aids are a huge public supply, and a no top-up device must be offered first.
entries.who_pays: Statutory health insurance pays for hearing aids. In 2024 that was 962,871 supplies.

entries.title: Clinic tools
entries.name: T16: Clinics / outpatient AgeTech
entries.summary: Shows health insurers are billed for outpatient care, but no ageing tool fee was named.
entries.who_pays: Practices bill health insurance for coded services. No fee code for a new tool was named.

entries.title: Heat and crises
entries.name: T17: Defense dual-use / resilience
entries.summary: Shows heat planning for health sits with states and towns, and is not a product tender.
entries.who_pays: States and municipalities hold the responsibility. No armed-forces purchase was found.

entries.title: Who pays for care
entries.name: T18: Berlin / DE ecosystem
entries.summary: Shows which German body pays for care, from care and health funds to medical review.
entries.who_pays: Care funds, health funds, and the medical review service are the bodies that pay or assess. They are not buyers of a startup product.

entries.title: Selling the family home
entries.name: P01: Property sale
entries.summary: Shows an adult child often starts a parent's house sale, while the parent still signs.
entries.who_pays: The owner pays the agent and the notary. Care insurance does not buy this.

entries.title: Inheritance at death
entries.name: P02: Inheritance at death
entries.summary: Shows at a parent's death the tax-free allowance and a left-out child's share come due.
entries.who_pays: The heir or the child would pay for advice. The tax office is not a software buyer.

entries.title: Leaving hospital
entries.name: P03: Hospital door
entries.summary: Shows the hospital must organise discharge, and the first prescription covers seven days.
entries.who_pays: The hospital already has the duty. It would pay only if it bought help to do that duty.

entries.title: Work at pension age
entries.name: P04: Employment contract
entries.summary: Shows a job can end at the standard pension age if nobody signs an extension.
entries.who_pays: The employer would pay for any paperwork. A care fund would not.

entries.title: Private health premiums
entries.name: P05: PKV premium
entries.summary: Shows a private health premium can jump at retirement when the employer share falls away.
entries.who_pays: The insured person pays the insurer. No euro gap was stated in the notes.

entries.title: Funerals
entries.name: P06: Cemetery
entries.summary: Shows in North Rhine-Westphalia the family must arrange the funeral, and the heir pays.
entries.who_pays: The heir pays. The municipality steps in only if the people who are obliged do not act.

entries.title: Gifts while alive
entries.name: P07: Gifts while alive
entries.summary: Adds a parent's gifts to a child together for tax across ten years.
entries.who_pays: The parent or the child would pay for advice. A care fund would not.

entries.title: Night hoist already there
entries.name: T01-H1
entries.summary: Shows a night shift with one carer may already be covered by the home's lift.
entries.who_pays: No new buyer. The care home already carries a shared lift in its care rate, not on a resident's invoice.

entries.title: Night care already stocked
entries.name: T01-H2
entries.summary: Shows the night shift may mostly be turning and pad care, using stock the home holds.
entries.who_pays: No new buyer. Stock for basic care sits with the home. The resident is not invoiced for a shared night routine.

entries.title: Which pad round to skip
entries.name: T02-H1
entries.summary: Shows the night nurse must decide who can skip one pad round without a skin injury.

entries.title: Wrong pad, missed delivery
entries.name: T02-H2
entries.summary: Shows a bad night may be the wrong pad size or a missed delivery from the pharmacy.
entries.who_pays: The pharmacy that supplies the care home is the buyer to test.

entries.title: Stopping one medicine
entries.name: T03-H1
entries.summary: Shows only a doctor and pharmacist can stop one of ten medicines, not a reminder app.

entries.title: Blister packs at night
entries.name: T03-H2
entries.summary: Shows the night trolley is poured from boxes when a personal blister pack did not arrive.
entries.who_pays: The pharmacy that packs the doses is the buyer to test.

entries.title: Who can enter
entries.name: T04-H1
entries.summary: Shows who may enter the flat in the first minutes is a private extra.
entries.who_pays: Entry in the first minutes is private extra cost, outside the 27 euro contract.

entries.title: After the second fall
entries.name: T04-H2
entries.summary: Shows the weeks after a second fall sit with a physiotherapy practice.
entries.who_pays: A physiotherapy practice is the buyer named for the weeks after a fall.

entries.title: A lab slip at check-up
entries.name: T05-H1
entries.summary: Shows people 65 and over may arrive at a check-up with a lab they paid for.

entries.title: Fit for this job
entries.name: T05-H2
entries.summary: Shows an employer may buy a test of job fitness that the check-up does not report.
entries.who_pays: The employer is the buyer named for a fitness-for-work test.

entries.title: Night wandering
entries.name: T06-H1
entries.summary: Shows an afternoon tablet misses night wandering that wakes the corridor.

entries.title: Alone after lunch
entries.name: T06-H2
entries.summary: Shows a working relative would pay a human to check on dementia after lunch.
entries.who_pays: A working relative is the person who would pay for a human check-in.

entries.title: Loneliness at midlife
entries.name: T07-H1
entries.summary: Shows the loneliness a programme can move may be at 43 to 55, not over 76.

entries.title: No visitor nearby
entries.name: T07-H2
entries.summary: Shows a free weekly visitor for people over 76 may not exist in that postcode.

entries.title: The bathroom never booked
entries.name: T08-H1
entries.summary: Shows the stair spends the grant, and the bathroom for home care never gets booked.

entries.title: The landlord says no
entries.name: T08-H2
entries.summary: Shows a landlord can refuse a fixed stair installation for a tenant.

entries.title: Tuesday's shopping
entries.name: T09-H1
entries.summary: Shows medical transport will not pay for the Tuesday shopping trip.
entries.who_pays: A municipality, through a tender, is the buyer named for everyday rides.

entries.title: The walk to the bus
entries.name: T09-H2
entries.summary: Shows medical transport is not asked to cover the walk to the bus stop.

entries.title: The order after choking
entries.name: T10-H1
entries.summary: Shows the ward may leave the meal order unchanged after a choking scare.

entries.title: Tell the swallow therapist
entries.name: T10-H2
entries.summary: Shows the speech therapist is never told which meal failed.

entries.title: A substitute this Friday
entries.name: T11-H1
entries.summary: Shows recognised help may have no free Friday slot in that town.

entries.title: The daughter's employer
entries.name: T11-H2
entries.summary: Shows an employer might pay when a daughter leaves work to manage the week.
entries.who_pays: The employer of a working daughter is the buyer named for navigation time.

entries.title: Replacing palliative records
entries.name: T12-H1
entries.summary: Shows only the palliative team, not the family, would buy replacement records.
entries.who_pays: The palliative team would buy the software. The health fund pays that team. A family subscription is refused.

entries.title: The prescribing practice
entries.name: T12-H2
entries.summary: Shows the practice that starts palliative care might pay for a handoff tool.
entries.who_pays: The doctor's practice would pay only if it buys software apart from the team's contract with the health fund.

entries.title: Help outside the VdK
entries.name: T13-H1
entries.summary: Shows families who are not members may still need help with a care grade.

entries.title: The assessment hour
entries.name: T13-H2
entries.summary: Shows no later software can put back the week the family did not show.

entries.title: Language for new staff
entries.name: T14-H1
entries.summary: Shows wages might pay recognition and language help for foreign care staff.
entries.who_pays: The employer pays from the wage bill. A care-fund subscription is refused. The worker is not the buyer.

entries.title: Hospital temp-staff rules
entries.name: T14-H2
entries.summary: Shows a hospital might pay for a temporary staff step a care home cannot take.
entries.who_pays: Hospital management would pay from the wage bill only if that rule leaves room for a vendor fee. The care-home cap does not.

entries.title: The free hearing aid
entries.name: T15-H1
entries.summary: Shows the hearing aid without a private top-up may not be offered first.

entries.title: No robot for activities
entries.name: T15-H2
entries.summary: Shows an activities lead may not rent a robot for an afternoon already staffed.

entries.title: Inside the practice system
entries.name: T16-H1
entries.summary: Shows a new practice function lives only if the system vendor ships it.

entries.title: Cash services, no code
entries.name: T16-H2
entries.summary: Shows a practice may take cash from people 65 and over for care with no fee code.
entries.who_pays: The patient pays the practice directly for a service the fee schedule does not contain.

entries.title: Heat exercise, no home
entries.name: T17-H1
entries.summary: Shows a heat exercise might reveal that crisis staff never name a care home.

entries.title: A heat plan at night
entries.name: T17-H2
entries.summary: Shows a heat plan can still fail at night with one nurse and no cooling.

entries.title: Who signs the invoice
entries.name: T18-H1
entries.summary: Shows a startup meeting is not the room that signs a care home invoice.
entries.who_pays: The care home operator is the person who would sign an invoice.

entries.title: A sale that stops
entries.name: T18-H2
entries.summary: Shows a national sale may not reach local groups that are legally separate.
entries.who_pays: Each local organisation would decide for itself.

entries.title: Child calls, parent signs
entries.name: P01-H1
entries.summary: Shows a child may call the agent, but only the parent can sign the house away.
entries.who_pays: The child might pay for advice or for an agent who acts for the owner. Care insurance is not this invoice.

entries.title: Settling the house early
entries.name: P01-H2
entries.summary: Shows children cannot split a future house without the owner and a notary.

entries.title: If you do not move in
entries.name: P02-H1
entries.summary: Shows if the child does not move in, only their 400,000 euro allowance remains.
entries.who_pays: The child might pay privately for advice. The tax office is not a software buyer.

entries.title: The left-out child's share
entries.name: P02-H2
entries.summary: Shows a child left out of the will is owed half the share by the heir.
entries.who_pays: The excluded child, or the heir who pays the claim, would pay. Not the care fund.

entries.title: The day after discharge
entries.name: P03-H1
entries.summary: Shows a hospital will not pay a second coordinator once the seven day prescription ends.
entries.who_pays: Only the hospital, and only if it buys help to perform a duty it already has.

entries.title: Refused hospital consent
entries.name: P03-H2
entries.summary: Shows refused written consent can leave only a claim on the health fund.
entries.who_pays: No vendor is named. The question is whether the health-fund claim still exists.

entries.title: The job still ends
entries.name: P04-H1
entries.summary: Shows a job can still end at pension age if nobody signs to extend it.
entries.who_pays: The employer would pay for the paperwork. A care fund would not.

entries.title: Rehire after leaving
entries.name: P04-H2
entries.summary: Shows the same employer cannot rehire a leaver on a fixed term with no special reason.

entries.title: Premium help ends
entries.name: P05-H1
entries.summary: Shows retirement can change the bill when employer help is not fully replaced.
entries.who_pays: The insured person pays if the replacement contribution is short. No euro gap was stated.

entries.title: Relief tariff, started late
entries.name: P05-H2
entries.summary: Warns a premium relief start near 65 can be late, and the extra premium remains.
entries.who_pays: The insured person pays the insurer. There is no new carrier.

entries.title: Who arranges the funeral
entries.name: P06-H1
entries.summary: Shows statutes put burial duty on the family and the bill on the heir.
entries.who_pays: The heir pays. It is not a care-fund invoice.

entries.title: Whose wish counts
entries.name: P06-H2
entries.summary: Shows a known will on burial or cremation beats the child's wish.
entries.who_pays: Whoever the burial rules and the heir's duty already name.

entries.title: Tracking gifts to children
entries.name: P07-H1
entries.summary: Shows tax adds up every gift from a parent to a child over ten years.
entries.who_pays: The parent or the child would pay privately. A care fund would not.

entries.title: Tax on a later gift
entries.name: P07-H2
entries.summary: Shows a later gift can be taxed more after earlier gifts used the allowance.
